title: 7 Academic Benefits Of Effective Classroom Management -management/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Following recent articles on declining post-pandemic behavior standards, Linsin turns to the direct academic case for classroom management, arguing it rivals content expertise as the single greatest driver of learning outcomes. He lists seven specific benefits: dramatically more time on task in a well-managed classroom; a culture where learning is treated as the central purpose of being present; the ability to focus deeply once interruptions and bullying threats are removed; the consistency that lets students build durable learning habits over time; the capacity to meaningfully challenge students without constant firefighting; accelerated maturity that compounds academic progress; and a generalized habit of behavioral success that transfers into every other domain. He closes by urging teachers to commit to becoming experts in classroom management, framing it as easier than most assume and as having a monumental, compounding effect on test scores, reading, writing, and math outcomes.
points: Classroom management is framed as rivaling content expertise as the single greatest driver of academic outcomes.
Well-managed classrooms produce dramatically more time on task, directly increasing the volume of learning.
Removing interruptions and bullying threats lets students focus deeply and get lost in the intrinsic joy of learning.
Consistency over time lets students build durable learning habits that can only develop in a calm, trusted environment.
A well-managed class can develop up to two years of extra maturity compared to a typical class, compounding academic progress.
quotes: Classroom management has always taken a backseat. Now it’s sitting in the trunk.
Along with a teacher’s expert knowledge of content, classroom management has the greatest impact on academic progress.
In an exceptionally well-managed classroom, students are focused and working for hundreds of more hours than a typical classroom.
They can get lost in the intrinsic joy of learning when they’re free from phones, social media, behavior disruptions, disrespect, chaos, and trying to be cool.
A well-managed class has a maturity level that grows throughout a school year to two years greater than the typical class next door.
Test scores, reading levels, writing and math abilities, work habits . . . you name it. All indicators of academic growth will skyrocket because of the undeniable, unstoppable benefits listed above.
